headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: next-ai-draw-io’s broad egress/MCP can expose Great Expectations outputs and amplify unverified content.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: great_expectations reads files such as validation results and documentation, while next-ai-draw-io uses natural-language commands plus MCP and browser-based workflows. If Great Expectations outputs are copied into draw.io workflows or MCP prompts, attacker-controlled content could steer instructions. The bridge is plausible but not documented directly.
conditions: IF Great Expectations output is pasted into next-ai-draw-io prompts or MCP inputs, prompt injection becomes plausible.
IF next-ai-draw-io parses imported text or diagrams as instructions, malicious content can steer tool use.
mitigations: Use a strict copy/paste boundary for any Great Expectations output.
Strip instructions from imported text before sending to next-ai-draw-io.
Disable MCP for untrusted inputs during review sessions.
requires-engineering: add provenance labels to imported artifacts.
requires-engineering: sandbox prompt parsing from file content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: great_expectations touches validation results and documentation, and next-ai-draw-io has broad network egress, multiple third-party model APIs, and handles API keys. If shared files or outputs flow from A into B, B can transmit sensitive validation data off-box by default. The pairwise leakage path is credible even without direct evidence of a shared workspace.
conditions: IF Great Expectations validation results contain sensitive data and are opened in next-ai-draw-io, those contents can reach external APIs.
IF the two agents share a workspace or copied files, B can exfiltrate A’s file contents through model calls.
mitigations: Keep sensitive validation outputs out of next-ai-draw-io.
Use local-only models for any imported Great Expectations artifacts.
Rotate or remove API keys before opening shared files.
Restrict network egress during review sessions.
requires-engineering: separate workspaces and enforce DLP on imported files.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: great_expectations can install packages and write files, while next-ai-draw-io supports multiple instances, browser use, MCP, and broad egress. Overlapping file-based workflows can conflict if both modify the same artifacts or environment variables, though the profiles do not prove a shared writable directory. Uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same project directory, file conflicts can occur.
IF next-ai-draw-io and Great Expectations share environment variables or package state, one can overwrite the other’s assumptions.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories.
Avoid concurrent edits to shared files.
Freeze package installs during paired runs.
Limit environment-variable sharing.
requires-engineering: add file locks or orchestration-level coordination.

D_cascading_error.rationale: great_expectations produces validation results that next-ai-draw-io can ingest through natural-language commands or file imports. If B treats A’s outputs as authoritative, a bad validation or malformed diagram can cascade into incorrect visualizations or downstream actions. The profiles show the handoff path, but not a verified verification step.
conditions: IF next-ai-draw-io uses Great Expectations validation results as authoritative input, errors can propagate.
IF imported diagrams or text are generated from unverified validation output, downstream artifacts may be wrong.
mitigations: Require manual review of Great Expectations outputs before import.
Compare imported results against source data summaries.
Mark generated diagrams as untrusted until checked.
Use a second validation pass for critical datasets.
requires-engineering: add verification gates between the agents.

E_compliance.rationale: great_expectations touches data quality tests, validation results, and documentation, while next-ai-draw-io handles PDFs, text, images, and API-key-backed cloud model calls. If regulated or sensitive documents are processed by B after A, retention and residency obligations may diverge. The profiles do not specify a DPA or residency controls, so uncertainty warrants medium.
conditions: IF regulated documents or PII are present in Great Expectations outputs and then opened in next-ai-draw-io, compliance obligations may diverge.
IF next-ai-draw-io sends imported content to third-party APIs, residency or retention rules may be violated.
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated data to cloud models.
Review retention settings before importing files.
Use redacted samples for diagram generation.
Document data-handling boundaries for both tools.
requires-engineering: implement residency-aware routing and retention controls.
